newsitem.title: USA: ComEd increasing power at Ill. nuke units.
newsitem.headline: ComEd increasing power at Ill. nuke units.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co said Friday it will generate more electricity at its three Illinois nuclear power units by early next week following repairs.
The 794 megawatt (MW) Dresden 2 nuclear unit, in Morris, Ill., will likely begin ramping up this weekend following testing of its turbine control valve, company spokesman Gary Wald said.
The unit has been operating at about 40 percent power for more than a week.
The 1,040 MW Zion 2 nuclear unit, shut since September, has begun startup and is expected to be on-line early next week, he said.
ComEd's Byron 2, with a generating capacity of 1,105 MW, was reduced to about 50 percent power Thursday night to replace a feedwater pump.
The unit, in Byron, Ill., is now holding at 75 percent power for testing and will likely begin ramping up later today or early Saturday.
Also, the 794 MW Dresden 3 nuclear unit is slated to restart January 13 after shutting down October 26 for maintenance.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
